case: stale MongoDB grid updates preserve concurrent field changes
outcome: MongoDB grid edits now compare the materialized original values of edited fields in the atomic update filter. Concurrent same-field changes produce zero matched rows and are preserved.
contract: Reads three documents through the BookiE MongoDB driver, then concurrently changes one payload, removes another document's explicitly NULL payload, and changes a third NULL payload to an array containing NULL through a native client.
Builds and executes the same value-keyed update shape used by the app materializer; all three stale updates return zero affected rows.
Checks the newer string value and sibling field remain stored, the concurrent field removal remains missing, and a concurrent array containing NULL survives.
Matches a BSON NULL guard only when the field exists and is not an array, preserving explicit NULL without matching missing fields or arrays containing NULL.
A failing-first run on the prior implementation matched one row and overwrote its newer value.

before_fix.result: failed as expected: matched_count was 1 instead of 0; the old filter only used _id

clippy.command: cargo clippy --locked -p tablepro-core -p tablepro-app -p tablepro-driver-mongodb --all-targets -- -D warnings

file_size.result: passed; the sql_dialect.rs baseline was reduced from 1205 to 1172

limitations: The field-value guard does not detect an ABA change that restores the original value.
Stale row deletes still match only the primary key and remain open.
This case does not establish snapshot isolation or qualify the 0.2.0 release.
